rules.title: How to play
rules.intro: Abalone is a game for two players on a hexagonal board of 61 spaces. Each side starts with 14 marbles and moves once per turn.

goal.title: The goal
goal.body: Push six of your opponent's marbles off the board. That is the whole game — there is nothing else to count.

directions.title: Six directions
directions.body: Every space touches six others, so a marble can move in any of six directions. There are no diagonals and no jumps — a marble always moves to a space right beside it.
directions.caption: The six directions open to a single marble.

move.title: Moving marbles
move.body: On your turn you move one, two or three of your own marbles. Two or three must sit next to each other in a straight line, and they all move one space in the same direction.
move.inline_caption: In line: the row advances along the direction it already points in.
move.broadside_caption: Broadside: the row steps sideways, and every space it lands on must be empty.

push.title: Pushing
push.body: Only a move in line can push. You need more marbles in that line than your opponent: two against one, three against one, or three against two. The space behind your opponent’s marbles must be empty.
push.ok_caption: Three against two — the whole line shifts one space.
push.blocked_caption: Three against three never moves, and you can never push your own marbles.

capture.title: Pushing marbles off
capture.body: A marble pushed past the edge is out for the rest of the game. The first player to knock six of the opponent's marbles off the board wins.
capture.caption: Two against one at the edge — the black marble is out.

local.title: Two players, one device
local.description: Black moves first, then the turn passes. Turn on board rotation in settings to flip the board for whoever is to move.
